extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of Euclidean geometry (geometers, mathematics students)
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpts of Euclid Book VI giving propositions that state when a triangle or parallelogram is 'given in species' (i.e., determined up to similarity) from various combinations of given angles, ratios, perpendiculars, segments, and applied parallelograms, together with constructive methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 3 (similarity from equal angle and ratio of drawn lines to bases)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two triangles ABC, LEF have one angle BAC equal to one angle ELF, and if straight lines drawn from these angles to the bases, making with them given and equal angles, have the same ratio to the bases, each to each; then the triangles are similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: draw perpendiculars from the equal angles to the bases; since one perpendicular is to its base as the other to its base, by earlier corollary the triangles are similar. Construction guidance follows: to find a triangle similar to ABC, describe a segment of a circle and use a line GH as in the proposition, find IK with the given ratio to EF equal to AD:BC, erect FK perpendicular to EF at F, compare FK to GH and draw a parallel to EF through K to meet the circumference; join points to form LEF similar to ABC. (Includes explanation about choosing K so the parallel meets the circumference and application of Cor.1.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. LXXVIII — rectangle of sides to square of base ratio (triangle given in species)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a triangle have one angle given, and if the ratio of the rectangle of the sides which contain the given angle to the square of the third side be given, the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof and construction: draw AD perpendicular to BC. From given angle BAC the ratio of triangle ABC to rectangle BA·AC is given; by hypothesis the ratio of BA·AC to BC^2 is given hence AD:BC is given, so triangle is given in species. Construction: take an arbitrary EF, make angle FEG equal to BAC, draw FH ⟂ EG and BK ⟂ AC; use similarity of ABK and EFH and set EF:FL equal to given rectangle:BC^2 ratio; then use Proposition 77 (or its construction) to find triangle OPQ with angle equal to BAC and altitude:base ratio equal to AD:BC; OPQ will be similar to ABC. An alternative analytic composition is also given using excess of squares and proportional composition (references to props 76 and 48).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. LXXIX — given angle and dividing line with given segment ratio (triangle given in species)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a triangle have a given angle, and if the straight line drawn from that angle to the base, making a given angle with it, divides the base into segments which have a given ratio to one another; the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: describe circumcircle of triangle, from centre draw radii to vertices; because angle at centre is double the given angle and BE:EC (radii) are known, triangle BEC is given in species; using ratios BD:DC and EB:BD (from given BD:DC) obtain triangles EBD and AED given in species and thereby the whole ABC. Construction: take a line given in position and magnitude, divide it in the given ratio for BD:DC, describe a circular segment containing the given angle BAC and from division point draw a line making the given angle ADB to meet circumference; join to form triangle similar to ABC. Alternative demonstration may follow Prop.77.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. LXXX — given ratio of sides about an angle and given altitude:base ratio (triangle given in species)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sides about an angle of a triangle have a given ratio to one another, and if the perpendicular drawn from that angle to the base has a given ratio to the base; the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two cases: (1) if AB = AC then AD bisects base BC and AD:BC (and hence triangle) is given. (2) If sides unequal (BA>AC), construct an auxiliary point E so triangles AEB and AEC are similar; deduce BE:EA and EA:EC from BA:AC and hence EB:BC and AD:BE from hypothesis; determine triangle ADE (right triangle) and then triangle ABE and thus ABC. Construction: to find such a triangle with given base GH and altitude K (equal to AD), form appropriate proportions (take K equal to altitude, choose GH as base), construct NM whose square equals sum of squares of NH and ML (ML=K) to locate points M,L and join to obtain triangle LGH. Detailed proportional and maximality arguments show existence and uniqueness conditions and how to vary ratio to obtain other triangles with same base and altitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. LXXXI — unequal sides about an angle with given ratio and altitude dividing base with given segment ratio (triangle given in species)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sides about an angle of a triangle be unequal and have a given ratio to one another, and if the perpendicular from that angle to the base divides it into segments that have a given ratio to one another, the triangle is given in species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: assume AB>AC, take point E with angle CAE = ABC so triangles ABE, CAE equiangular; deduce proportional relations BE:EA, EA:EC from BA:AC and from BD:DC derive ratios for EC:CD and DE:EA; ADE is right so triangle ADE is given; then triangles AEG and BEA given yield angles ACB and ABE, hence ABC given in species. Note requirement: ratio BA:AC must be less than BD:DC; construction: take base GH given, divide it at K and L so GK:KH equals BA:AC and GL:LH equals BD:DC, draw LM ⟂ GH and construct circle centered N with radius NK intersecting LM to give O such that triangle OGH has required ratios. The text shows how to place L between K and H and construct with mean proportionals and circle intersection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. LXXXII — parallelogram increased/diminished by a gnomon: sides of gnomon given
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parallelogram given in species and magnitude be increased or diminished by a gnomon given in magnitude, the sides of the gnomon are given in magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case 1 (increase): AB given in species and magnitude, gnomon ECBDFG given → whole AG given in magnitude and in species (similar to AB) so its sides AE, AF etc. are given; remainders EC, DF are then given. Case 2 (diminish): AG given in species and magnitude diminished by gnomon ECBDFG; remaining AB is given in magnitude and species hence its sides CA, AD given and remainders EC, DF given. Construction: given the target figure H to be formed by gnomon, find a parallelogram similar to AB equal to AB+H, place its sides and take away common part to obtain gnomon equal to H; analogous steps for diminution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. LXXXIII — apply parallelogram equal to given space, deficient by given parallelogram (sides of defect given)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parallelogram equal to a given space be applied to a given straight line, deficient by a parallelogram given in species, the sides of the defect are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction/analysis: bisect AB at E; on EB describe parallelogram EF similar to the given defect DL; EF is given in species and magnitude and about same diameter; EF diminished by the given gnomon ELH yields sides EK, FH of the gnomon given; EK = DC and FH = DB, hence CD and DB are each given. The demonstration is noted as the analysis of a prior problem (Prop. 18 of Book 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. LXXXIV — apply parallelogram equal to given space, exceeding by given parallelogram (sides of excess given)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parallelogram equal to a given space be applied to a given straight line, exceeding by a parallelogram given in species; the sides of the excess are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure mirrors LXXXIII: bisect AB, describe EF similar to LD on EB; EF is given in species and magnitude, EF increased by gnomon ELH equal to given figure AC gives sides EK and FH which equal CD and DB respectively; thus CD and DB given. The proposition is the analysis of the relevant construction (29th prop, Book 6). A corollary: if a parallelogram given in species be applied to a given straight line exceeding by a parallelogram equal to a given space, the sides AD, DC of the parallelogram are given (construction given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. LXXXV — two lines containing given parallelogram; difference given (each line given)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two straight lines contain a parallelogram given in magnitude, in a given angle; if the difference of the straight lines be given, they shall each of them be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let AB, BC contain parallelogram AC given in magnitude in angle ABC, and let DC be given equal to excess of BC above BA. Complete parallelogram AD. Because AB = BD and angle ABD is given, parallelogram AD is given in species; with AC applied to DC exceeding by AD (given in species) the sides of the excess are given, hence BD is given; DC is given, so whole BC is given and AB is given. Construction follows from applying the earlier proposition about applying parallelograms and sides of defect/excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. LXXXVI — two lines containing given parallelogram; sum given (each line given)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two straight lines contain a parallelogram given in magnitude, in a given angle; if both of them together be given, they shall each of them be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let AB, BC contain parallelogram AC in given angle ABC and AB+BC be given. Produce CB, make BD = AB and complete parallelogram ABDE. Parallelogram AD given in species; since AB+BC is given and AB = BD, DC is given; apply AC to DC deficient by AD (given in species) and by Prop. LXXXIII the sides of the defect are given, so BD and thus AB, BC each given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. LXXXVII — two lines containing given parallelogram; excess of squares given (each line given)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two straight lines contain a parallelogram given in magnitude, in a given angle; if the excess of the square of the greater above the square of the lesser be given, each of the straight lines shall be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let AC be parallelogram given in magnitude in angle ABC. Let the given excess of BC^2 above BA^2 be represented by rectangle CB·BD. Subtract this from BC^2 to get rectangle BC·CD equal to BA^2; using ratios from the given angle and parallelogram, the rectangle AB·BC is given and rectangle CB·BD is given. From these construct ratios that yield DB:BA and hence squares and compositions leading to BC and BD being given. Composition (construction): give an explicit construction using auxiliary figure EFG and rectangles EG·GH and HG·GL to form mean proportionals and set up ratios so that parallelogram AC equals given rectangle EG·GH and the excess of squares equals HG·GL. The demonstration is the analysis of the associated problem and composition is given in the text (details involve mean proportionals, doubling, and bisecting).
